## Reply to DaviTostes and slint6614-dev (conflict and #442)

Thanks for flagging this. I merged current upstream main (ffe310e) into the branch in 3bc83d0 (a merge, no rebase or force push). The conflict in crates/victory-shader/src/emit/lower.rs was in `inputs()`: main changed the SGPR arm to `Reg::S(n)` for uninitialized SGPRs, and this PR added an arm that loads barycentric VGPRs lazily. Both arms are kept. The merge also needed one small follow-up: the barycentric test helper now passes the structure to `resource::track`, which takes it as a fourth argument on main.

About #442: it is not in main yet (its head, b6ccc95, is not an ancestor of main, and main has no SV_Barycentrics code), so there was nothing to reconcile in this merge. The two PRs do overlap: both map signature kind 28 to semantic 23, set the Barycentrics feature bit, and read I/J as SV_Barycentrics. Whichever lands second should be rebased on the first so there is a single SV_Barycentrics path. I'm happy to do that on this side if #442 goes in first.

## Reply to marquezinii and r4tedx (two perspective modes)

Thanks for the validator report and the pointer. I could not find commit 55c2938 in the PR refs or the forks I can fetch, so I wrote a fix on my side: 88b34a4.

DXIL allows at most two SV_Barycentrics elements, one perspective and one linear. A program that read both perspective center and perspective centroid I/J as values declared two perspective elements. Now the second perspective mode (or the second linear mode) is refused with a clear Unsupported reason ("barycentrics of two perspective modes (SV_Barycentrics allows one)"), and no second element is declared. I chose to refuse instead of reusing the single element: centroid weights stay inside the triangle and center weights do not, so on edge pixels reusing one for the other would give a silently wrong value. Before this PR, those reads were refused anyway, so nothing that worked before regresses. Interpolating attributes with both modes through the normal `v_interp` path is not affected, because that still uses host interpolation.

There is a new test, `center_and_centroid_barycentrics_are_refused`. It fails without the fix (the program translates with two perspective elements) and passes with it. One caveat: the tests' `validate()` silently passes when dxil.dll does not load, so these tests only check the validator on a machine where it loads.
